philosophy.name: Zahabi
philosophy.rule: ~70% sustainable effort, more often, beats occasional maxing. Don't max lifting and skill on the same day.
philosophy.apply: Most rounds at a pace you could repeat tomorrow. Heavy lift day ≠ hard sparring/drilling day.

philosophy.name: Danaher
philosophy.rule: Systemize. Go deep on a few high-percentage families, not a thousand techniques.
philosophy.apply: Striking: jab-cross-hook family + slip/parry. Grappling: double leg → top control → back → RNC. Master the chain before adding branches.

philosophy.name: GSP
philosophy.rule: Integrate disciplines until switching between them is automatic.
philosophy.apply: Every striking round ends with a level change; every grappling round starts from a striking stance.

philosophy.name: Daru Strong
philosophy.rule: As skill volume rises, S&C volume drops. Fix dysfunction (feet, mobility) before loading it.
philosophy.apply: Boxing lesson weeks → lift 2x not 3x. Short-foot + Screw work before heavy single-leg loading.

philosophy.name: Topuria
philosophy.rule: Train striking and grappling together, rotate weekly emphasis blocks, build the engine with roadwork plus sprints.
philosophy.apply: 4-week rotation below; 2 roadwork/sprint sessions per week.

contactLadder.name: Shadow
rules: Mirror or phone video for feedback.

contactLadder.name: Pads / Mitts
rules: Partner holds, you hit. Light-to-medium power.
Holder keeps elbows soft and pads close to the face line — no slapping into punches.

contactLadder.name: Cooperative Drilling
rules: Pre-agreed attack + defense (e.g. partner jabs slowly, you slip and counter to the body).
~20% speed, zero head contact on the sibling.
Grappling: drill entries and positions with no resistance.

contactLadder.name: Light Live Grappling
rules: Positional rounds only (e.g. start in side control), 1–2 min.
Tap early, tap often. No neck cranks, no slams, no heel hooks.
Adult supervision if the partner is younger/smaller.

contactLadder.name: Controlled Sparring
rules: Rare — at the boxing gym with a coach, not at home.

drills.name: Stance Lock
drills.cue: Screw both feet into the floor — knees soft ~25°, chin down, hands at the cheekbones.

drills.name: Step-and-Stick
drills.cue: Land balanced, feet same width every time.

drills.name: Jab from Stance
drills.cue: Front foot pushes the floor, fist turns over at the end — snap it back to the cheek.

drills.name: Jab on Mitts
drills.cue: Hit through the pad by 2 inches, then return faster than you went out.

drills.name: Hip Snap Cross
drills.cue: Back heel turns out, hip turns first, fist arrives last — like cracking a whip.

drills.name: Med-Ball Rotational Throw
drills.cue: Same chain as the cross: ground → hips → core → shoulder → ball.

drills.name: Hook off the Pivot
drills.cue: Pivot the front foot, elbow stays at shoulder height, body turns the punch — the arm is just the hook.

drills.name: Push-Step Box
drills.cue: Push off the opposite foot; never cross feet.

drills.name: Pivot Out
drills.cue: Turn on the lead ball of the foot to step off the line.

drills.name: Slip Line
drills.dose: 3 × 1 min under a string or partner slow jabs (Level 2)
drills.cue: Bend at the knees and turn the shoulders — eyes stay on the chest.

drills.name: Parry Drill
drills.cue: Small hand movement — redirect, don't reach.

drills.name: Object-Approach Tracking
drills.dose: 2 × 20 soft ball tosses toward the face, catch or slip
drills.cue: Watch it all the way in — teaches your brain incoming objects are safe (threat suppression).
Weight shifts back-front-back; each punch loads the next.

drills.name: Jab-Cross-Slip-Cross
drills.cue: The slip loads the hips for the counter.

drills.name: 1-2 to Level Change
drills.cue: Punches raise their guard; the shot goes under it.

drills.name: Level-Change Reps
drills.cue: Drop the hips, not the head — chest up, Screw feet.

drills.name: Sprawl
drills.cue: Hips slam to the floor, legs back, chest heavy.

drills.name: Penetration Step
drills.dose: 3 × 10 per side (solo or on a mat)
drills.cue: Knee lands between their feet, head up, drive off the back foot.

drills.name: Double-Leg Entry on Partner
drills.cue: Ear on hip, hands behind knees, turn the corner.

drills.name: Position Climb
drills.cue: Half → side → mount → back: each step, heavy hips, chest-to-chest.

drills.name: Shrimp Lanes
drills.cue: Bridge into them, then push your hips away with your feet.

drills.name: RNC Mechanics
drills.dose: 3 × 5 per side (Level 2: set up only, no squeeze on sibling)
drills.cue: Elbow under chin, hand to bicep, other hand behind their head — squeeze elbows, don't crank the neck.

weeklyBlocks.notes: 3 striking skill days, 1 grappling day. Lift 2x. Roadwork 2x.
3 grappling days (drilling, positional), 1 striking day. Lift 2x.
Every session mixes: strike → level change → top control. Lift 2x, lower volume.
Skill at 70%, Norwegian 4×4 + sprints, lifting reduced to 1–2 crisp sessions.

conditioning.name: Interval Warm-Up (EIB)
conditioning.dose: 6 × 30 s hard / 30 s easy before every hard round session
conditioning.why: High-intensity interval and variable warm-ups reduced post-exercise FEV1 drop (Stickland 2012).

conditioning.name: Roadwork
conditioning.why: Aerobic base speeds recovery between rounds.

conditioning.name: Sprints
conditioning.dose: 6–8 × 10–15 s hill or treadmill, full walk-back recovery
conditioning.why: Top-end speed and repeat-effort capacity (Topuria-style engine).

conditioning.name: Shadowboxing Rounds
conditioning.why: Sport-specific conditioning; holds technique under fatigue.

safety: Default with younger sibling: levels 0–2 only.
Mouthguard for anything with contact; gloves on both people for pads.
Tap early; any neck pain, headache, or dizziness = stop for the day and tell a parent.
No head contact at home. Body-only targets in cooperative drills.
Sharp or joint-line pain mid-drill: stop and swap the drill.
